subject: Creativity
title: Dieter Rams: The 10 Principles of Good Design
description: A quick, practical guide to Dieter Rams: The 10 Principles of Good Design.

hook.text: Jony Ive's Apple designs look like Dieter Rams's Braun products from the 1960s. That's not coincidence — it's reverence.

buildup.text: Rams set 10 principles: good design is innovative, useful, aesthetic, understandable, unobtrusive, honest, and lasting.

discovery.text: His most radical principle: 'Good design is as little design as possible.'

twist.text: He designed the Braun T3 radio in 1958. Compare it to the iPod — same proportions, same minimalism, 43 years early.

climax.text: At 91, Rams says design has failed — too much waste, too much planned obsolescence.

punchline.text: Good design removes everything unnecessary. What remains is honest.

quiz.question: Which of Rams's principles states design should remove everything unnecessary?
options: Good design is as little design as possible
